title_ja: 元営業職員による金銭の不正な取得に関する調査終了について
title_en: Conclusion of investigation into improper acquisition of money by a former sales representative
summary_en: Meiji Yasuda Life announced on 21 June 2024 that it had finished its investigation into a former sales representative at its Shinjuku branch who took customers' money improperly. The case came to light on 18 October 2021, and the conduct began in February 1994 and happened repeatedly. It affected 5 households (10 people) for about 130 million yen, mainly through unauthorized policy loans and misappropriated prepaid premiums. The total includes the 2022 case of about 20 million yen. The insurer said it would keep strengthening compliance controls over its sales representative channel.

The report follows the Life Insurance Association's "points of focus" guidance. The Association issued that guidance in February 2023 and updated it in April 2024 with reference examples. The report sets out the company's main measures so far and the direction of its future efforts, organised by the guidance's items. The release itself gives no new rules or effective dates. The detail is in a linked PDF.
